facts.raw_span: A 73-year-old man presented with intractable hiccups
His past medical history included fatigue several years prior
he received chemotherapy (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, vincristine, and prednisone) followed by autologous peripheral blood stem cell transplant
Serial monitoring thereafter revealed normal complete blood cell counts
The patient was afebrile with normal vital signs
Neurologic examination findings were normal except for the presence of hiccups
Brain MRI with gadolinium showed: Diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement
Enhancement of several cranial nerves including bilateral vagus nerves
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed: Lymphocytosis with plasmacytoid features on light microscopy
Flow cytometry showed κ light chain–restricted B-cell lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation

Nodular enhancement involving cisternal segments of bilateral glossopharyngeal and vagus nerves, right hypoglossal nerve, intraparenchymal ventral medullary enhancement, and extensive leptomeningeal enhancement
Follow-up showing improvement after treatment

concepts.why: The presence of lymphocytosis with plasmacytoid features in the cerebrospinal fluid and the flow cytometry results showing κ light chain–restricted B-cell lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation support this diagnosis.
The diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement and the enhancement of several cranial nerves, including bilateral vagus nerves, are consistent with leptomeningeal metastasis.
The combination of lymphocytosis with plasmacytoid features in the cerebrospinal fluid and the flow cytometry results, along with the neuroimaging findings, supports this diagnosis.
The presence of hiccups and the enhancement of the vagus nerves on neuroimaging suggest vagus nerve dysfunction.
The presence of hiccups and the nodular enhancement involving the glossopharyngeal nerve suggest glossopharyngeal neuralgia.
The diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement and the presence of hiccups could be related to intracranial hypotension.
The patient's history of rituximab treatment and the development of lymphocytosis with plasmacytoid features in the cerebrospinal fluid support this diagnosis.
The patient's history of chemotherapy and the presence of hiccups and neuroimaging abnormalities suggest a chemotherapy-related neurological disorder.

rationales.F01: Intractable hiccups suggest CNS involvement, which is consistent with central nervous system lymphoma and neurolymphomatosis.
rationales.F03: Rituximab is associated with an increased risk of lymphoproliferative disorders, which could explain the patient's symptoms.
rationales.F06: Normal neurologic examination findings except for hiccups suggest a localized lesion, which is consistent with central nervous system lymphoma and neurolymphomatosis.
rationales.F07: Diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement on MRI is a characteristic finding of central nervous system lymphoma and leptomeningeal metastasis.
rationales.F08: Enhancement of cranial nerves, including the vagus nerve, is consistent with neurolymphomatosis and vagus nerve dysfunction.
rationales.F09: Lymphocytosis with plasmacytoid features on CSF analysis is a characteristic finding of central nervous system lymphoma.
rationales.F10: Flow cytometry showing κ light chain–restricted B-cell lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation is diagnostic of central nervous system lymphoma.
rationales.F11: Nodular enhancement involving cranial nerves and leptomeningeal enhancement is consistent with neurolymphomatosis and central nervous system lymphoma.
